hints: Focus on what controls size here, nuclear charge pulling on the same shells of electrons, and whether the particles are neutral atoms or ions.
Notice that $\text{N}^{3-}$, $\text{O}^{2-}$, $\text{F}^{-}$ and also $\text{Na}^{+}$, $\text{Ne}$, $\text{F}^{-}$ are all isoelectronic with 10 electrons, so size depends only on proton number.
For isoelectronic particles, more protons means stronger pull and smaller size, so order them by falling proton number to get smallest to largest.
walkthrough:
**Recall two different size trends**

Think like a teacher with you. For neutral atoms across a period, more protons pull the same shell in tighter, so size decreases. For ions with the same electron arrangement, the same idea applies even more strongly.

Rule: more protons for same electrons = smaller particle.

**Check row A, neutral atoms N, O, F**

These are Period 2 atoms with nuclear charges 7, 8, 9. The pull increases from N to F, so atomic radius decreases.
$$\text{N} > \text{O} > \text{F}$$
So A is largest to smallest, not smallest to largest.

**Check isoelectronic rows B, C and D**

All the particles in B are $\text{N}^{3-}$, $\text{O}^{2-}$, $\text{F}^{-}$ with 10 electrons but protons 7, 8, 9. Fewest protons means weakest pull, so $\text{N}^{3-}$ is largest and $\text{F}^{-}$ is smallest. Row B shows the reverse order.

Similarly in C, $\text{Na}^{+}$, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, $\text{Al}^{3+}$ all have 10 electrons with protons 11, 12, 13, so size decreases across the row:
$$\text{Na}^{+} > \text{Mg}^{2+} > \text{Al}^{3+}$$

**Confirm row D is correct**

In D, $\text{Na}^{+}$, $\text{Ne}$, $\text{F}^{-}$ all have 10 electrons with protons 11, 10, 9. Falling nuclear charge means increasing size.
$$\text{Na}^{+} < \text{Ne} < \text{F}^{-}$$
This exactly matches smallest to largest.

options.A: Incorrect. Across Period 2, effective nuclear charge increases from N (7 protons) to F (9 protons), pulling the outer shell closer. So size decreases N > O > F, the opposite of smallest to largest.
options.B: Incorrect. These three ions are isoelectronic (all have 10 electrons). With the same repulsion, the fewest protons gives the largest ion. Actual order is F- < O2- < N3-, so the row is written backwards.
options.C: Incorrect. These three ions are also isoelectronic (all have 10 electrons). Proton numbers increase 11 to 13, so attraction increases and size decreases. Actual order is Al3+ < Mg2+ < Na+, the opposite of the row.
options.D: Correct. Na+, Ne and F- are isoelectronic with 10 electrons but with 11, 10 and 9 protons respectively. Decreasing nuclear charge means less pull on the same electron cloud, so size increases from Na+ (smallest) to Ne to F- (largest).
